Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To show the state of one thing next to its name: in a tile, a row, a header or a table cell.
  • For a maturity scale or workflow stage, with each step mapped to one tone (see Content rules).

When not to use

  • For a message that needs a sentence or an action: use cmp-inline-alert.
  • For a count or a category label without a state: use plain text (ds-text-caption).
  • As a button or filter: a status pill is never interactive.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • neutral — not started, inactive or unknown: a grey dot.
  • info — in progress or under review: a blue dot.
  • success — done, ready or healthy: a green dot.
  • warning — needs attention soon, or partly done: an amber dot.
  • danger — blocked, failed or at risk: a red dot.

Anatomy

  • Root: <span class="ds-status-pill ds-status-pill--<tone>"> holding the word.
  • Dot: drawn by the component before the word in the tone's mark colour; it is decoration, so the word must say the state on its own.
  • Every tone shares one quiet neutral fill and the muted text colour, so a row of pills stays calm and only the dots carry colour.

Accessibility

  • The word is the state; the dot only repeats it, so the state is never told by colour alone.
  • The pill is plain text to assistive technology. When the word needs context ("Ready" of what?), the surrounding row or heading provides it, or the pill reads as a phrase ("Review: blocked").
  • The pill's text meets AA on its fill in every theme (text-muted on neutral-surface).

Interaction

  • Not interactive: no hover, focus or press. When the state changes, the word and dot change at once; nothing animates unless the change itself is the news (int-04, int-06).

Content rules

  • One or two words in sentence case: "Ready", "In review", "Blocked".
  • Use the same word for the same state everywhere in the product.
  • A four-step maturity scale maps, in order, to neutral, warning, info and success. For example: Placeholder is neutral, Mock is warning, Draft is info and Ready is success.

Do and don't

  • Do place the pill right after the name it describes, on the same line.
  • Do keep one pill per item; show history elsewhere.
  • Don't invent a sixth tone or colour a pill to decorate.
  • Don't put a pill inside running text; rewrite the sentence instead.
